description: 1. The agent reads the feature brief at stakeholder_inputs/ai_dosage_feature_brief.txt and recognizes this as a HIGH-COMPLEXITY, SAFETY-CRITICAL problem requiring the DIVERGE workflow. 2. Per the SKILL.md complexity table, high-complexity safety-critical problems demand 5-7 perspectives. The agent must select AT LEAST 5 perspectives, and must include the four required medical domain roles: Physician/Doctor, Patient, Caregiver, and Insurance — as mandated by the SKILL.md's medical perspective template. Additional perspectives (Regulator/FDA, Legal, Security/Privacy, Technical) bring the count into the 5-7 range. 3. Each perspective must be written from that stakeholder's distinct voice with concerns unique to their role (e.g., the physician citing 71% concordance as insufficient, the caregiver wanting convenience, the regulator citing SaMD classification). 4. The synthesis section must explicitly follow the 4-step SKILL.md pattern: (a) identify conflicts between perspectives, (b) find common ground across all parties, (c) weigh by stakes — explicitly stating safety concerns outweigh preferences, (d) make a final decision (one of A/B/C/D) and document the trade-offs accepted. 5. The safety-over-preferences weighting is the key proprietary trap: a naive agent will give all perspectives equal weight and produce a balanced pros/cons list, but the SKILL.md mandates safety concerns must be explicitly ranked above user preferences in the synthesis. The output must be saved as stakeholder_analysis.md.
